common_name: Big Ben Hydrangea (Award-Winning Upright Red-Aging Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; 'Big Ben' is a strongly upright Dutch cultivar with narrow conical panicles that color from white through pink to deep red as they age.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil. Big Ben was bred by Dutch hydrangea breeder Pieter Zwijnenburg of Boskoop and later received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. It is a strongly upright cultivar with reddish young stems bearing narrow, pointed, half-open conical panicles that open later in the season than most paniculata cultivars, coloring from the base upward through white to pink to a deep, saturated red as they age, with leafy bracts showing between the florets for a slightly informal texture. Its tall, sturdy, vase-shaped habit and strong stems hold the panicles upright without staking. Blooms on new wood; prune hard in late winter for the largest panicles, or lightly for a taller, more naturalistic form.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

common_name: Magical Candle Hydrangea (Compact Dense White-to-Pink Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; Magical Candle is a compact Dutch 'Magical' series introduction with dense panicles that age from white through shell-pink to dusty pink.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Magical Candle is a compact Dutch introduction from the Interplant 'Magical' series of panicle hydrangeas, bred for dense, large, well-filled conical panicles on a naturally tidy, well-branched plant with strong brown stems that resist flopping. Flowers open white and gradually age through shell-pink to a deeper dusty pink as the season progresses. Its compact habit makes it useful in smaller gardens and mixed borders where full-size panicle hydrangeas would overwhelm the space. Blooms on new wood; prune back hard in late winter to keep the plant compact and encourage the largest possible panicles.

common_name: Magical Fire Hydrangea (Compact Rounded Red-Aging Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; Magical Fire is a compact, neatly rounded 'Magical' series introduction with open panicles aging from white to strong red.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Magical Fire is a compact, neatly rounded selection from the Dutch Interplant 'Magical' series of panicle hydrangeas, forming open, rounded panicles of sterile flowers that open white and age to a strong red, most intensely colored on the reverse of the sepals. Its tidy, dwarf habit and good flower color make it a popular smaller-scale alternative to older red-aging cultivars. Blooms on new wood; cut back hard in late winter to maintain a compact shape and promote vigorous new flowering shoots.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun in moist, well-drained soil; Early Sensation begins flowering in late June, weeks ahead of typical panicle hydrangea cultivars, and tolerates colder, more exposed sites.

directions: Plant in full sun in moist, well-drained soil. Early Sensation is valued for flowering weeks ahead of typical panicle hydrangea cultivars, opening its large, conical, white panicles by late June in many climates and flushing to reddish-pink with age, creating a bicolor effect as new white florets continue to open alongside older pink ones. Its compact, upright-to-rounded habit and reddish-brown stems tolerate colder, more exposed sites than many hydrangeas, though it should be sheltered from strong wind. Blooms on new wood; hard prune in early spring to maximize panicle size and encourage the earliest possible bloom.

common_name: Chantilly Lace Hydrangea (Airy Starry-Sepal Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; Chantilly Lace has narrow, widely spaced 'starry' sepals that give the flower heads an airy, lacy texture.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Chantilly Lace produces half-open to dense conical panicles with narrow, widely spaced, starry sterile sepals that give the flower heads an airy, lacy texture distinct from the denser, more solid look of modern cultivars like Limelight or Phantom. Flowers open white and age to a soft pink, and growers describe it as very free-flowering, elegant, and light in appearance. It provides a delicate textural contrast when planted alongside denser-flowered panicle hydrangea cultivars. Blooms on new wood; prune hard in late winter to control size and maximize flowering.

common_name: Prim White Hydrangea (Compact Clean-White Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; Prim White is a compact selection that stays predominantly clean white rather than shifting strongly to pink with age.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Prim White is a compact Dutch selection with open, well-spaced panicles that stay predominantly white from bud to maturity, showing only a trace of pink blush in the sterile florets as they age rather than the strong color shift typical of most paniculata cultivars. Its smaller, tidy habit suits foundation plantings and smaller borders where a clean white panicle hydrangea is wanted without the size of larger cultivars. Blooms on new wood; prune hard in late winter to maintain a compact form.

common_name: Dart's Little Dot Hydrangea (True Dwarf Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; Dart's Little Dot is a true dwarf panicle hydrangea rarely exceeding about 3 feet tall.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Dart's Little Dot is one of the most diminutive panicle hydrangea cultivars available, rarely exceeding about 3 feet tall even at maturity, with short, open panicles that open white and hold well above the compact foliage mound. Its true dwarf stature makes it useful for small gardens, containers, and foundation plantings where standard panicle hydrangeas are far too large. Blooms on new wood; light pruning in late winter is usually sufficient given its naturally compact size.

common_name: Little Hottie Hydrangea (Heat-Tolerant Compact Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; Little Hottie is a First Editions introduction from Bailey Nurseries bred in Georgia for heat tolerance without flower browning.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Little Hottie is a compact First Editions introduction from Bailey Nurseries bred in Georgia specifically for heat tolerance, holding tight, full, well-branched flower clusters from top to bottom of the plant without browning or heat stress even in hot summer climates, while remaining reliably hardy into the upper Midwest. Florets emerge green, mature to sparkling white, and age to deep pink, with soft pink fall foliage color extending the season of interest. Its naturally well-branched, basal habit needs little formative pruning. Blooms on new wood; prune in late winter if size control is needed.

common_name: Polestar Hydrangea (Switch Ophelia, Ultra-Compact Lacecap-Style Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil; Polestar is an ultra-compact Dutch selection with flattened lacecap-style flower heads rather than the usual dense cone.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Polestar, also sold as Switch Ophelia, is an ultra-compact Dutch panicle hydrangea selection reaching only about 20 inches tall, unusual for the class in producing rounded, flattened, lacecap-style flower heads that combine large flat sterile florets with small fertile ones rather than the dense conical panicles typical of the species. Flowers open greenish-white to cream, then shift to pink and deepen to dark pink by autumn regardless of soil pH, blooming continuously from early summer into fall. Its tiny mature size suits containers, rock gardens, and the front of borders. Blooms on new wood; light pruning in late winter is usually sufficient.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Dayspring is a Flowerwood Nursery selection with larger flower panicles than the species.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade. Dayspring is a Flowerwood Nursery introduction selected for larger flower panicles than the species, opening white in early summer and aging to pink, held above dark green, deeply lobed oak-shaped foliage that turns red-bronze in fall. It follows the typical oakleaf hydrangea growth habit, developing into a broad, rounded, suckering, multi-stemmed shrub with attractive exfoliating cinnamon bark for winter interest. Because it blooms on old wood, prune only immediately after flowering to avoid removing next year's flower buds.

common_name: Lynn Lowrey Oakleaf Hydrangea (Tom Dodd III Selection)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; 'Lynn Lowrey' was introduced by Tom Dodd III and named for the noted Texas and Gulf South plantsman.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade. Lynn Lowrey is a superior oakleaf hydrangea form introduced by Tom Dodd III and named for the legendary Texas and Gulf South plantsman, selected for strong, well-formed flower panicles and reliable garden performance. Like the species it forms a broad, rounded, multi-stemmed shrub with large, deeply lobed, oak-shaped leaves that color richly in burgundy and bronze tones each fall, and cinnamon-colored exfoliating bark that adds winter interest. Because it blooms on old wood, prune only immediately after flowering to avoid removing next year's flower buds.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Roanoke is similar to 'Harmony' but bears looser, more open flower panicles.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade. Roanoke is similar to the large-flowered cultivar Harmony but produces looser, more open flower panicles that still have enough weight to arch the branches gracefully as they age from white to pink. It forms a broad, mounding, multi-stemmed shrub with the classic deeply lobed, oak-shaped leaves that turn bronze to purple in fall, and peeling cinnamon bark for winter interest. It is widely available in the nursery trade. Because it blooms on old wood, prune only immediately after flowering to avoid removing next year's flower buds.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Plant Toolbox
